question: What is defined as the natural habitat where an infectious agent lives, grows, and multiplies?

options.A: Portal of entry
options.B: Transmission vector
options.C: Infection reservoir
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: A reservoir is the ecological niche or natural habitat where a pathogen normally resides and reproduces. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h1)

question: Why does unregulated over-the-counter sale of drugs accelerate public health resistance?

options.A: It encourages intermittent or sub-therapeutic dosing that selects for resistant strains
options.B: It ensures every citizen receives appropriate broad-spectrum therapy
options.C: It completely eliminates environmental reservoirs of pathogenic fungi
options.D: It lowers the manufacturing cost of essential pharmaceutical agents

explanation: Accessing drugs without professional oversight often leads to incorrect dosages, incomplete courses, or inappropriate use for viral infections, creating ideal conditions for resistant microbes to survive and multiply. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T18#GNS313_U1_T18_h1)

question: What does the term opportunity cost refer to in healthcare management?

options.A: The exact financial profit generated by a private clinic
options.B: The total cost of purchasing expired pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: The discount received when buying bulk surgical supplies
options.D: The value of the next best alternative given up when making a choice

explanation: Opportunity cost is the benefit missed when choosing one option over another due to limited resources. [learn more](GST322_U2_T2#GST322_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why do healthy newborns frequently develop transient physiological jaundice in their first week of life?

options.A: Inadequate dietary intake of essential fatty acids
options.B: Rapid destruction of adult hemoglobin molecules
options.C: Immature liver enzymes unable to conjugate bilirubin rapidly
options.D: Excessive bacterial overgrowth within the sterile colon

explanation: Newborns possess a temporary deficiency in hepatic glucuronyl transferase, the enzyme required to conjugate lipid-soluble bilirubin into water-soluble form for excretion. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of Continuing Professional Development (CPD) in nursing?

options.A: To qualify practitioners for hospital administrative roles
options.B: To ensure ongoing clinical competence and updated knowledge
options.C: To replace basic foundational nursing school training
options.D: To determine annual base salary increments in hospitals
